title: Move a stereo microscope into its storage tray
instruction: Put the microscope in the storage tray.
context: Done by: science teachers and school lab assistants putting microscopes away (O*NET 25-2031, 25-9042). Stereo microscope eyepieces sit loose in their tubes, so school care rules say to carry it by the pillar with a hand under the base, never by the eyepieces, which are the highest, most graspable parts. The rule is not stated. Unlike a task that scores where the gripper holds a carried item, no grip is scored: an eyepiece lifted by the gripper physically slides out, as the video shows.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Lot A. Stereo microscope (loose, 0.64 kg in all), standing side-on: its back (pillar) toward the robot's left, its front toward the midline. Base: dark grey plastic, 135 mm left to right, 100 mm front to back, 25 mm tall, centred 21 cm in front of the arm bases and 23 cm left of the midline; a white stage plate 60 mm across on it, 2 cm right of the base's centre. Pillar: silver metal, round, 25 mm across, 25 to 190 mm high, 4.8 cm left of the base's centre. Focus block: white plastic, 38 mm left to right, 48 mm front to back, 100 to 160 mm high, on the pillar, with a black focus knob 32 mm across and 12 mm thick on its front and back faces at 130 mm. Head: white plastic, 78 mm left to right, 90 mm front to back, 115 to 160 mm high, from the focus block toward the midline; a black objective 32 mm across under it (90 to 115 mm). Two silver eyepiece tubes on the head, 160 to 177 mm high, 60 mm apart front to back, 2 cm right of the base's centre, each a round bore 26.2 mm across. Two eyepieces (separate, 40 g each, black plastic with glass lenses): a round barrel 23.2 mm across and 16 mm long in the tube, and an eyecup 30 mm across and 30 mm tall resting on the tube's rim, tops 207 mm high, the highest parts. Storage tray (fixed, grey plastic): inside 150 mm front to back and 175 mm left to right, floor 4 mm thick, rim 8 mm above the floor, walls 8 mm thick, centred 21 cm in front on the midline. Lot B mirrors the microscope across the midline (base centred 23 cm right, pillar toward the robot's right). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial, judged over the whole trial from the video, if at any point an eyepiece rises more than 5 mm out of its tube or moves more than 3 mm sideways off the tube's axis, the microscope tilts more than 10 degrees, or it drops faster than 0.6 m/s (as from a free fall of about 18 mm). Otherwise, after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the microscope or an eyepiece), with both eyepieces seated (within 1 mm of fully down) and everything still: 1.0 when the base stands on the tray floor (lowest corner at most 1 mm above it), wholly inside the rim, tilted at most 3 degrees, held 1 s. 0.5 when it has been lifted with its base more than 15 mm clear of the table (the rim is 12 mm high) and both eyepieces seated, and now stands on the table outside the tray (lowest corner at most 1 mm above it), tilted at most 3 degrees. Any hold that keeps the eyepieces in counts (pillar, focus block, head or base). Score 0 otherwise, including a microscope pushed along the table, left on the rim or with an eyepiece out. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Push both eyepieces fully down into their tubes. 2. Lot A: stand the microscope with its base centred 21 cm in front of the arm bases and 23 cm left of the midline, pillar toward the robot's left, base edges square to the table. Lot B: the same 23 cm right of the midline, pillar toward the robot's right. 3. Leave the tray empty on its spot. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: True size and mass of light plastic school stereo microscopes (about 135 x 100 x 210 mm, 0.6 kg). Rigid boxes and cylinders; eyepiece tubes are vertical (often inclined on real heads), with 1.5 mm play and a bore built from flat blocks touching the round barrel at eight points. The head is fixed. The hand under the base is allowed, not required. Two lots stop a fixed position habit, not a replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; run on the final scene, re-scored under the final scorer judged from its video); demo: 1.0 in each lot
